metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Nebraska (2026):Rules, Exemptions & Examples

description: Nebraska base sales tax is 5.5%. Most gold, silver, platinum, and palladium bullion is exempt; jewelry and non-bullion numismatic collectibles may be taxable.

What's covered by the exemption
Gold/silver/platinum/palladium bullion generally exempt
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Nebraska.
Is gold, silver, platinum, or palladium bullion taxable in Nebraska?
+
No. Nebraska generally treats precious-metal bullion as fully exempt from sales tax.
Are numismatic coins taxed in Nebraska?
+
It depends. Nebraska distinguishes bullion from numismatic collectibles, so non-bullion numismatic items may be taxable.
Does the bullion vs. collectible classification matter in Nebraska?
+
Yes. Whether an item is treated as bullion or a non-bullion collectible helps determine if the exemption applies.
Is jewelry taxable in Nebraska?
+
Yes. Precious-metal jewelry is taxable under Nebraska sales tax rules.
Do local Nebraska taxes generally follow the state bullion exemption?
+
Typically yes. Nebraska generally follows the state rule for bullion, though local tax administration can still affect checkout calculations.
